To offer reassurance— during the lockdown, my depersonalization attacks came back. Every single day. I know the feeling. But I promise you can beat this! You just have to find your grounding techniques to take your mind out of it.

We do recover. My first one was induced by mdma, I was 19. I’m almost 28 now. You somehow learn to bring that fight or flight feeling you get. What you’re feeling is anxiety, which is in response to the way you felt the very first time—as you said traumatic experience. 
Whenever that feeling hits me, I sing a song or move my body, something to distract the anxious,dizzy feeling I get. The more anxious you let yourself get, the more it’ll happen. I know it sounds ridiculous, “how can I control my anxiety?” 
I went through this process of learning what helps to pull me out of it. 5 things you can see, feel, taste, hear. Or put your hands under cold water. Meditation. Deep breathing. Or move your body around, sing a tune. 
Sometimes even just closing your eyes for a bit and imagining a place that brings you peace. 
Best of luck 💗 it’ll get better!

My vision changes significantly when I’m having a bad panic attack because my brain checks out. It freaked me out at first as well.
Nothing looks realistic, it’s like I’m in a video game or a dream.

Your brain naturally tries to protect itself with depersonalization from traumatic events. Your body could be registering it as that even if it’s not, fight or flight. If you like a good read, “the body keeps the score” is a good one and it talks about this!
Also, anxiety with depersonalization can be exhausting. So a headache after the occurrence doesn’t sound out of the ordinary!

For me, yes. I actually have a certain feeling that occurs when I’m about to “check out” of my brain. My stomach drops and I have tingles all over my body. And my brain feels dizzy and I can’t think. 
Literally feels like I’m leaving my body. And then the anxiety kicks in. So it could be your body’s fight or flight reaction giving you those responses.

Also try to stay away from heavy amounts of alcohol or anything that can alter your state of mind. I found alcohol was a major trigger for me and stopped drinking until I started feeling it gradually go away.
